samples.summary: `mergeInlineStyle` deleting cleared keys silently changes what "Clear formatting" renders on styled (heading/title) blocks in the MemDocStore path
samples.evidence: Before this diff, `{ ...inline.style, ...resolvedStyle }` left every `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` key *present with value `undefined`* on the stored run. Style resolution is `{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }` (`view/layout.ts:156`, `model/range-runs.ts:64`), and an explicitly-present `undefined` overrides the named-style default. So in the memory store, Ctrl+\ on a Heading 2 used to suppress the style's fontSize 16 / colour (rendering at the 11pt theme fallback) and on a Heading 6 also suppressed `italic: true`. With the new `delete merged[key]`, those defaults now show through — clear formatting on a Heading 6 leaves the text italic, and heading sizes/colours survive the clear. This is outside the stated scope of the change (`docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md` scopes item 2 to the toggle path) and nothing pins it: `packages/docs/test/view/editor-clear-formatting.test.ts:109-113,142` only asserts `toBeUndefined()`, which passes either way. Mitigating: `YorkieDocStore` already removed the attributes (`removedInlineStyleAttrs` → `removeStyleByPath`), so production docs behaviour was already the new one; the visible change is confined to MemDocStore surfaces (slides/docs text boxes, demo, tests).

samples.summary: Toggle-off clears only the boolean, leaving `underlineStyle`/`underlineColor`/`strikeStyle` as dead companion keys, so the stated "run re-merges" goal fails for such runs
samples.evidence: `BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS` covers only the six booleans. `inlineStylesEqual` (`model/types.ts:409,412`) also compares `underlineStyle`, `underlineColor` and `strikeStyle`, so a run whose underline came with a variant (set by the pptx importer, `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:499,511`) still cannot re-merge with its neighbour after `underline: false` is demoted to a clear, and the orphaned variant keys remain as run-level overrides that a later named-style redefinition cannot reach — exactly the #749 residue class the change targets. Toggling underline back on then reads the stale variant.

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` demotes *any* `false` in the patch, not just a fresh toggle-off, so a deliberately carried "off" override can be dropped
samples.evidence: The predicate is only `style[key] !== false`; it cannot distinguish a toggle-off from a `false` the caller is deliberately propagating. Reachable via the format painter: `TextEditor.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }` (`packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869`) captures the raw run style, which for a Heading 6 run legitimately contains `italic: false` (the retained-override case this diff creates). Applying that buffer to a paragraph (`text-editor.ts:1013` → `applyStyleToSelection` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle`) now clears the key instead of storing it; if that paragraph is later converted to Heading 6 or a style redefined to be italic, the painted "not italic" silently flips to italic. Visually identical at write time, so low impact, but it is an information-losing rewrite of a patch that was not a toggle-off.

samples.summary: Yorkie optimistic cache now re-merges runs the CRDT tree keeps split, widening cache↔tree structural divergence after every boolean toggle-off
samples.evidence: `applyStyle` updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper` (which now clears the key, so `normalizeInlines` merges the three split runs back into one) while `applyStyleInTree` leaves three inline nodes in the Tree (merging them is an explicit non-goal in the task doc). Before the change the stored `false` kept the cache split too, so the two agreed. The store's own offset resolution is tree-based (`resolveBlockNodeOffset`), so I could not find a concrete corruption path, but one place does derive an index from the cache — `const cacheResolved = resolveOffset(block, offset); const targetInline = block.inlines[cacheResolved.inlineIndex]` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1570-1571) — and the document a caller reads flips its inline count (1 vs 3) depending on whether the cache or a fresh tree parse served it, which is the kind of instability the unlink lessons doc warns about.
